children: Automaker Stellantis N.V. (STLA, Financials) behind Jeep, Ram, Fiat and Peugeot, may be readying to streamline its operations as it prepares for a bigger investment cycle.
The firm is said to be considering selling its controlling position in used-car marketplace Aramis Group.
Stellantis owns 60.5% of Aramis and controls 67.4% of the voting rights. Rothschild & Co and Citi have reportedly been hired to work on a prospective sale.
The stats tell us how much things have changed since Aramis went public. The firm is now valued at just 263 million, down from nearly 1.9 billion at its 2021 IPO.
Also, business has eased. Sales of Aramis vehicles plummeted more than 6% to 1.6 billion in the first nine months of 2026, with restored vehicle sales down about 5%.
The prospective exit comes as management focuses more on Stellantis' main automotive business.
The automaker is planning investments of almost 60 billion up to 2030 in the face of growing competition, mainly from Chinese manufacturers. Stellantis shares increased roughly 3.4% on Thursday.
Next to monitor is what the rumored Aramis sale proceeds, and what additional noncore businesses Stellantis might decide it doesn't need anymore.

title: Stellantis Is Starting to Decide What It No Longer Needs
